 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Draymond Green and Al Horford will start Wednesday’s game against the Rockets. 
 The Warriors are going with a more traditional lineup to start Wednesday’s game, with Horford getting his first start of the season. Gui Santos, whose minutes have been limited recently due to a knee injury, will come off the bench. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  NBA Lineups

 Al Horford 
 GSW 
 Center 
 #20 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Al Horford (back) is available for Thursday’s game against the Heat. 
 Horford is available after sitting out Monday’s win over the Suns, which was the Warriors’ second game in as many nights. While he will provide frontcourt depth off the bench, Horford should not be rostered in fantasy leagues at this stage of his career. 
 Al Horford 
 GSW 
 Center 
 #20 
 Al Horford (back) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Horford had nine points, five rebounds and two assists in 22 minutes off the bench against the Clippers on Sunday. He’ll sit out the second game of a back-to-back against the Suns Monday, though his absence won’t impact fantasy basketball. 
 Al Horford 
 GSW 
 Center 
 #20 
 Al Horford (back) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Horford has not played both games of a back-to-back in a few years. So his absence from the injury report for Sunday’s game means he’s unlikely to play Monday against the Suns. 
 Draymond Green 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Draymond Green (back) and Al Horford (back) are available for Monday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 Neither Green nor Horford played in Saturday’s loss to the Suns. The former’s absence opened a starting spot for Gui Santos, who exited in the third quarter with a leg injury and did not return. Green will return to his usual starting role, with Horford providing bench depth. 
 Al Horford 
 GSW 
 Center 
 #20 
 Al Horford (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Suns. 
 Horford is out with back injury management. Purely a depth piece at this stage of his career, Horford isn’t likely to play enough minutes to be fantasy-relevant even when he’s healthy. 
 Graham Ike 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #45 
 Graham Ike produced 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 After starting Draymond Green at center in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr opted against that approach on Friday. As a result, Ike made his first NBA start. The rookie from Gonzaga shot reasonably well, but he offered little value beyond points and three-pointers. The Warriors visit Phoenix on Saturday, and Ike may play more, as Al Horford hasn’t played both games of back-to-backs in a few years. 
 Charles Bassey 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Charles Bassey (knee) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Bassey did not play in Wednesday’s opener against the Lakers, leaving the Warriors light on options at center. With Kristaps Porziņģis (illness) out indefinitely, Draymond Green may spend more time at center than head coach Steve Kerr would prefer. Al Horford can provide depth off the bench, but he’s unlikely to exceed 20 minutes. 
 Charles Bassey 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Charles Bassey (knee) is out for Wednesday’s matchup with the Lakers. 
 With Kristaps Porzingis (illness) sidelined, the Warriors will have to rely on Draymond Green and Al Horford at center, offering rookie Yaxel Lendeborg the opportunity to see significant minutes right out of the gate. On the other side of the court, Walker Kessler could be in for a huge night against Golden State’s shorthanded and undersized frontcourt rotation. 
 Charles Bassey 
 GSW 
 Forward-Center 
 #28 
 Charles Bassey (knee) is questionable to play against the Lakers on Wednesday. 
 Bassey showed some juice during the preseason and may be part of the rotation as a depth big man when he’s healthy. If he’s not available for this game, Al Horford will likely take on a few extra minutes, with Draymond Green spending most of his time at center. 
 Al Horford 
 GSW 
 Center 
 #20 
 Al Horford tallied 15 points (5-of-8 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Trail Blazers. 
 Horford, who is expected to play around 20 minutes per game during the regular season, logged 15 minutes on Friday. That was all he needed to put up quality offensive numbers, shooting 5-of-8 from beyond the arc. Even with Kristaps Porziņģis out indefinitely due to illness, Horford’s limited minutes aren’t enough to make him a viable option in standard fantasy leagues.

 Player Stats

 Amen Thompson recorded 19 points (8-of-11 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and two blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors.
 Thompson remains a valuable fantasy option, especially for managers willing to punt three-pointers. However, his scoring average has decreased by more than three points per game compared to last season. Thompson’s ability to fill a stat line has preserved most of his value. However, he’ll need to be a more productive scorer to live up to his top-25 ADP. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Alperen Şengün produced 19 points (8-of-14 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), 13 rebounds, nine assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors.
 In 10 games this season, Şengün has recorded six double-doubles and one triple-double. His fantasy value has also been boosted by improved efficiency, with the Rockets center shooting over 50 percent from the field and posting higher averages in points, rebounds, and assists. Turnovers can still be an issue for Şengün on occasion, but he committed just two against the Warriors. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Kevin Durant 
 HOU

 Kevin Durant shot 8-of-17 from the field and 3-of-4 from the foul line in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors, scoring 20 points with four rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer.
 Durant led six Rockets in double figures on Wednesday, and he’s scored at least 20 points in four straight games. Given his career résumé, that isn’t a significant achievement for KD. That said, he’s been more aggressive offensively than he was earlier in the season, which is good for those rostering Durant. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darryn Peterson got himself 22 points (7-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, and two 3-pointers in 123-108 loss to the Magic. 
 Over the past week, Darryn Peterson has gotten more confident, aggressive, and the Jazz have been letting him lose. The peripheral stats from college have started to come back, and it’s been exciting to watch. You want more in terms of efficiency, but with Lauri Markkanen out for a month, Darryn is a must roster if he hasn’t been picked up in your league already.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Ace Bailey put up 18 points (6-of-17 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, four blocks, and three 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday. 
 Ace Bailey has been great this season and has been one of the best shot blockers in the NBA. His ability to havoc defender at this point is a great sign for his long-term development. He’s coachable and is a great teammate. The efficiency wasn’t great in this one, but it’s hard to complain with the peripheral stats that he gave you in this one.

 Brice Sensabaugh has had a rough month of November, but it was good to see a bounce back game from the scoring department. Sensabaugh kept the Jazz afloat in the fourth quarter on the offensive end when the Magic shut off the water on everyone else. He remains a stream guy for points and 3’s in redraft leagues, but not a high priority one.
